skill.name: brewpage-publish
skill.description: Publish text, Markdown, JSON, local files, and built static sites to brewpage.app with configurable expiry and optional password protection.
skill.summary: Create shareable brewpage.app links and save owner tokens in local project history.
skill.author: kochetkov-ma

security_audit.summary: The static alerts match documentation, defensive exclusions, and expected publishing operations rather than demonstrated malicious behavior. Context review found unsafe history destinations, conflicting token-disclosure instructions, unattended privacy defaults, and unbounded ZIP inspection. No evidence found of deliberate credential theft or encoded executable payloads.

remediation.issue: The old-publication recovery guidance contradicts the prohibition on printing owner tokens.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the instruction to report the owner token; require recovery replies to contain only the URL and local history location.

remediation.issue: Token-history destinations can follow symlinks and permission failures do not stop publication.
remediation.suggestion: Reject symlinked history paths and parents, create history atomically with mode 0600, and abort if ownership or permission checks fail.

remediation.issue: Adding a gitignore entry does not protect history that is already tracked.
remediation.suggestion: Detect tracked history with git ls-files and refuse token storage until the file is removed from the index.

remediation.issue: Missing answers permit publication without password protection.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit access-policy approval before upload; allow unattended publication only through a separately supplied, deliberate authorization flag.

remediation.issue: ZIP integrity testing can consume unbounded local processing time.
remediation.suggestion: Reject oversized archives before testing, enforce entry and expansion budgets with a structured ZIP parser, and apply child-process timeouts.

semantic_findings.title: Owner-token history follows repository-controlled paths
semantic_findings.description: History writes follow symlinks, and chmod failures are ignored. A crafted checkout can redirect owner tokens outside the intended private history file.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code checks -f but never rejects symlinked history files or parent directories. Redirection and chmod follow these paths before token append.

semantic_findings.title: Unanswered privacy prompts permit unprotected publication
semantic_findings.description: Missing namespace and password answers default to an unlisted link without authentication. Unattended runs can publish selected content without explicit access-policy approval.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow explicitly treats no answer as permission to use an unlisted namespace and no password. Publication is intended, but privacy consent fails open.

semantic_findings.title: Archive integrity checks lack local resource limits
semantic_findings.description: Supplied ZIP files undergo decompression testing before upload without a timeout or expansion cap. A malicious archive can exhaust local CPU or stall inspection.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: unzip -tq processes archive contents synchronously with no timeout. maxBuffer limits captured output, not decompression work or expanded bytes.

semantic_findings.title: Recovery guidance conflicts with owner-token confidentiality
semantic_findings.description: The recovery note says "report the new URL and owner token", contradicting the explicit prohibition on conversational token disclosure. Following it could expose management credentials.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both conflicting instructions appear verbatim in the skill. Exposure depends on agent interpretation; the script does not itself print owner tokens in normal results.

content.user_title: Publish Files and Static Sites to Brewpage
content.value_statement: Sharing a document or static site often requires hosting setup. This skill uploads selected content to brewpage.app and returns a shareable link.
actual_capabilities: Detect local files, directories, ZIP archives, JSON text, and text destined for Markdown rendering.
Upload text, JSON, files, and static site archives to the corresponding brewpage.app endpoints.
Package directories with an extension allowlist while excluding hidden entries, dependency folders, and symlinks.
Inspect ZIP integrity, print archive manifests, select an entry page, and request confirmation for flagged filenames.
Configure namespace, requested expiry, delivery mode, and password headers sourced from an existing local file.
Save returned owner tokens and publication metadata in project history without printing tokens in normal results.
limitations: Uploads require network access, Bash, curl, and jq; sites also require Node.js and unzip, with zip needed for directory packaging.
Hosts built static content; it does not build projects or run server-side applications.
Filename checks do not inspect file contents for secrets, and unlisted links remain accessible without a password.
Service limits and existing publication expiry control retention; the command does not implement owner updates or deletion.

use_cases.title: Share a review document
use_cases.description: Publish an approved report file with a short expiry and return its exact sharing link.

use_cases.title: Deploy a static prototype
use_cases.description: Upload a built interface with its assets, choose the entry page, and review the archive manifest.

use_cases.title: Distribute sample JSON
use_cases.description: Validate and publish sanitized example data for collaborators without creating a dedicated hosting project.

prompt_templates.title: Publish a short note
prompt_templates.prompt: Publish this exact text to brewpage.app: Release review starts Monday. Ask me to approve visibility and password settings before uploading.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: share a short text note.

prompt_templates.title: Share a local report
prompt_templates.prompt: Publish my approved report file with a one-day expiry. Show its size and ask me to confirm access settings before uploading.

prompt_templates.title: Publish a built static site
prompt_templates.prompt: Publish my selected build directory as a site. Use index.html, show the manifest, and stop if sensitive filenames require confirmation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: deploy built output with an explicit entry.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect and protect a ZIP site
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect my selected site ZIP and check current limits. Ask for namespace, expiry, and an existing password-file path before upload; never print credentials.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: review an archive and configure protected publication.

output_examples.input: Publish an approved report with a one-day expiry.
output: Published: the exact link returned by brewpage.app.
Owner token saved in the project history file.
The unlisted link can be opened by anyone who has it unless password protection was selected.

output_examples.input: Publish a built static site using index.html.
output: Archive manifest lists the selected web assets and skipped entries.
Published site: the exact service link, preserving its trailing slash.
Entry: index.html. File count comes from the service response.

output_examples.input: Inspect a site archive containing a filename marked as sensitive.
output: Confirmation required: review the flagged archive entries.
Nothing uploaded. Choose whether to publish anyway or cancel.

best_practices: Publish only reviewed build output or sanitized documents; inspect file contents for embedded credentials before sharing.
Explicitly approve visibility and password settings; use short retention for temporary material.
Check the history destination for symlinks and tracked files, protect owner tokens, and preserve the exact returned publication URL.
anti_patterns: Publishing source repositories or sensitive material because filename filtering appears sufficient.
Treating an unlisted namespace as authentication or accepting unattended password defaults for confidential content.
Uploading untrusted archives without resource controls or assuming expiry makes disclosure harmless.

faq.question: Which content types can I publish?
faq.answer: The workflow supports text rendered as Markdown, JSON text, individual files, built static directories, and existing site ZIP archives.

faq.question: Does publication require an account?
faq.answer: The documented workflow publishes without an account. Sign-in is optional and is not required by the scripts.

faq.question: Is an unlisted namespace private?
faq.answer: It avoids the public gallery and indexing, but anyone with the link can open it unless password protection is enabled.

faq.question: How does password protection work?
faq.answer: Provide an existing local password file using its absolute path. The script sends a password header without printing the password.

faq.question: Where is the owner token stored?
faq.answer: It is saved to .claude/brewpage-history.md at the project root. Check destination safety and Git tracking before trusting its intended protections.

faq.question: Can this skill build or update my application?
faq.answer: It uploads existing static output but does not build applications. The bundled command does not implement owner updates or deletion.
